page: Microsoft Azure FX4-2mds_v2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads, delivering 2 vCPUs at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions). The server is configured with 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 42.0 GB per core, and includes 236 GB of local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The high 4.2 GHz clock speed drives top-tier single-core Geekbench scores of 2342.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.72 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.32 GB/sec). However, due to the low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, with a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2884.0 and a poor stress-ng multi-core CPU performance rating. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds categorized as poor at 21.11 GB/sec and 14.3 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4-2mds_v2 provides a specialized hardware profile that prioritizes massive memory capacity and high single-core CPU frequency over parallel processing power. This resource density makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not scale across many cores but require substantial RAM, such as small-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks. It is less suitable for heavily multi-threaded applications, large-scale web serving, or parallelized compilation tasks.
